summary: This assessment focuses on transistor-level threats and mitigations for digital gates used in secure computations, emphasizing side-channel leakage and fault injection vulnerabilities.

threats.deployment_consequence: Reducing side-channel exposure is significantly harder post-deployment due to embedded nature of hardware.
threats.description: Transistors within digital gates can inadvertently leak information through observable power and electromagnetic signatures while switching states.
threats.potential_impact: Compromise of sensitive computation data via side-channel analysis.
threats.priority_rationale: High priority due to the critical nature of the information that can be leaked and difficulty in fixing this post-manufacture.
threats.scenario: An attacker measures power consumption to retrieve secret computation states during encryption operations.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: This threat arises from the physical layout and electrical characteristics established during the transistor design and must be mitigated at the implementation stage.
threats.title: Side-Channel Leakage Due to Switching Behavior

threats.deployment_consequence: Mitigating power sensitivity requires substantial redesign; retrospective patching is impractical.
threats.description: Transistor gates may malfunction under controlled power variations, allowing attackers to induce faults into computations, especially cryptographic operations.
threats.potential_impact: Triggering incorrect states in cryptographic procedures, resulting in potential bypasses or information leakage.
preconditions: Ability to vary power supplied to the device
threats.priority_rationale: Critical due to ease of execution in deployment and potential for severe operational impacts.
threats.scenario: An attacker induces faults in a gate's operation by modulating the power supply voltage.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: Faults from power variations are best identified and designed around during manufacturing controls, where defects and variability can be tested and minimized.
threats.title: Fault Injection via Power Supply Manipulation

threats.deployment_consequence: Difficult to detect and correct after deployment without comprehensive monitoring or replacement strategies.
threats.description: Transistor gates can degrade over the lifespan of the device, leading to parameter shifts that affect performance and reliability, possibly causing unintended faults during critical operations.
threats.potential_impact: Slow degradation of operation leading to sporadic failures and potential data corruption.
preconditions: Extended operational period under suboptimal conditions
threats.priority_rationale: Medium priority as it progresses slowly and impacts continuity more than confidentiality.
threats.scenario: Gate threshold drift over time leading to incorrect logic levels during computation.
threats.sdlc_phase_description: This concern emerges during long-term operation, particularly in environments with high temperature variations or continuous usage.
threats.title: Aging-Induced Failure Over Lifetime
